doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: Publishing royalties and unrecouped record costs at Warner Brothers
summary: Fleck earned publishing money while record royalties did not appear for ten years, until after eight Warner records. Other artists rarely record his music because it is so personal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: The fellows that I talked to that were recording in the forties say basically the same thing, that they never made much money off the records, if any.

Well there was a period where it seemed like I was making a ton of publishing money. But we’d never see any actual royalties. Because the publishing money comes from the first record. If you write a song and maybe it’s a song that somebody, it’s not even your song. So they have to pay that person. They can’t hold that money up. Like they can hold the artist’s money up on a record because whatever it cost to make a record they could say well I’m not going to pay you, Sonny Rollins. I’m not going to pay you until your record costs are paid off. And then they can manipulate the numbers so that it never happens or it happens and you just never know. But with the writer’s royalties they have to come from the very first record sold. So I found that I was making good money from writer’s royalties and seeing no record — none of the records went into — like at Warner Brothers it wasn’t until after eight records and like a year or two after the eighth record came out that the whole account paid off. So for ten years there was no income whatsoever from actual record sales. But the fact that we were writing all this music we were seeing a lot. So we knew they were making a lot of money. And it was like 700,000 records or more on Warners, and we never saw any. But we also took the budgets. The budgets were considerable too.
It must be nice when people from other groups and so forth, record some of your music that you’ve written.
It doesn’t happen very much. I can’t think of —
It doesn’t happen very often. It’s pretty rare. But for our stuff, because it’s just such personal stuff.
But I love it. Love to see that happen.
